rulings.chains: a direct chain is an iter() call or std::iter::range(a, b), any number of skip(n)/take(n) calls, and one consumer: count, sum/product::<i64|u64|f64>, collect::<Vec|Object|Tuple|String>, or next()/a for loop after at least one adapter; it is expanded into charged instructions over the existing IterNext, Binary and Branch, with adapter counts in slots
rulings.refusals: iterators stored in variables, passed or returned keep their earlier refusal; VecDeque, HashSet and HashMap collections and function values of range stay refused at compile time
rulings.providers: each consumer and adapter is certified as installed by the std Iterator trait on every iterator a chain can reach (slice, Object, Option, the nine range iterators, Skip and Take); range as the std iter module function; next and the for-loop protocol through the C14b Next certificate
rulings.range: std::iter::range(a, b) is the iterator (a..b).iter() after the stock i64 argument conversions (u64 accepted, Bad argument #0/#1); stored, it reaches only the existing for and next paths
rulings.texts: overflow ("Numerical overflow"), element conversion, argument conversion and tuple texts copied from stock exactly
rulings.seed: sum/product convert the first element as the seed in the turbofish type (so [-0.0] sums to -0.0); an empty chain gives that type zero or one
rulings.laziness: adapter counts convert in source order when each adapter is reached; take stops without pulling, skip pulls and discards; elements are converted only when consumed
rulings.key_copy: collect::<Object> copies each String key and leaves the key handle readable, in both engines since S2
rulings.fuel: fuel is charged per expanded instruction: rows that exhaust stock fuel halt in fresh with the stock class (C14b Retained-fuel precedent)
rulings.warnings: stock LetPatternMightPanic for a destructuring for pattern; the fresh frontend does not report it (O1 precedent)
rulings.arity: a wrong operand count is refused at compile time (stock: runtime ArgumentCount)
rulings.wrong_receiver: fresh names the missing method (existing D1 intentional diagnostic)
